taskReview.previewUnavailable: Exact writer output is unavailable. Meaning acceptance requires an existing UID and a valid single-document patch.

taskReview.noSemanticDelta: This request does not change the parsed meaning. No meaning decision record is needed.

limit.title: This agent has hit its usage limit
limit.hint: Not the app: the agent's own plan is out of room. If "Details" names when it resets, press "Try again" then; until then pick another agent below and carry on.
limit.hintOnlyTool: Not the app: the agent's own plan is out of room, and it is the only agent set up here. If "Details" names when it resets, press "Try again" then. Connecting a second agent on the Agents screen gives you somewhere to carry on.

auth.title: Saved sign-in has expired
auth.hint: You do not need a separate sign-in. This app uses the same one you use in your terminal. What is in the way is a keychain entry from an earlier app-only sign-in: it hides the shared one and has already expired. Press "Try again" below and the app clears that entry and falls back to your real sign-in. If that still fails, paste the one-line command under "Details" into a terminal.

install.title: An interrupted download left broken files
install.hint: The first-run download was cut off halfway, and the leftover files make it fail at the same spot every time. Press "Try again" below and the app clears them and downloads again from scratch. Check your internet connection and keep the app open while it downloads (a few hundred MB).

timeout.title: The agent is not responding
timeout.hint: Nothing came back from the agent for 45 seconds. A download in progress keeps the wait alive, so this is closer to a real stall. Press "Try again" below. If it keeps happening, check that the agent starts on its own in a terminal.

launch.title: The agent could not be started
launch.hint: Agents shows what state this agent is in. The button below opens it.

network.title: Cannot connect to the network
network.hint: Check your internet connection, then press "Try again" below. Reading and editing the map works offline.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.hint: Press "Try again" below. If it keeps happening, what is under "Details" is what to report.

connectSource.label: Connect the code folder first
connectSource.prompt: Connect the code folder that actually implements this project first. Do not analyze vault files as source code before it is connected.

bootstrap.label: Read the code and start the map
bootstrap.prompt: Start building the ontology from the connected source code. First orient with connection_info and list_kinds. Propose domains, capabilities, implementation elements, and evidence paths from the source; look for similar existing concepts first and write nothing before I review it. Write only the candidates I approve as a batch, then report validate_vault and compile_ontology results.

island.label: {count} items including “{firstLabel}” are not connected to anything else. Find where they should connect
island.prompt: {count} concepts including “{firstLabel}” ({first}) are not connected to the rest of the map. Using the code as evidence, work out where they belong and propose the links along with why.

containment.label: The “{slugLabel}” document says it belongs to “{domainLabel}”, but the “{domainLabel}” document’s list does not include “{slugLabel}”. Check which side is right and make the two documents agree
containment.prompt: “{slugLabel}” ({slug}) says it belongs to “{domainLabel}” ({domain}), but the domain-side link is missing. Check whether that home is right, and align both sides if so.

evidence.label: {count} capabilities do not say which code implements them yet. Start with “{firstLabel}” and find that code
evidence.prompt: Run query_ontology('{operation: "maintenance_plan", kinds: ["capability_without_evidence"], limit: 3}'), then inspect “{firstLabel}” ({first}) first. These {count} capabilities have no implementation file path and no linked element written down yet. Find the implementation evidence and propose the smallest path or element update. Do not write before I review it, and say when no evidence can be found.

explain.label: Explain what this folder does from the map alone
explain.prompt: Using only the {count} concepts on the map and their relations, explain to a newcomer what this folder is. Invent nothing that is not on the map, and point out any place the explanation stalls, because that is a hole in the map.

explainSubject.label: Explain what “{subject}” does from its record and relations
explainSubject.prompt: Read “{subject}” ({slug}) with get_concept and find_neighbors, then explain what it does, what it belongs to and what it relies on. Use only what the folder records; where the record is silent, say so rather than guessing.

subjectImpact.label: Find what a change to “{subject}” would reach
subjectImpact.prompt: Starting from “{subject}” ({slug}), use find_backlinks and find_neighbors to list the concepts a change to it would reach, each with the relation that carries it. Write nothing; end with the one place you would check first and why.
